entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Muhammad Said Shamil, also referred to in the North Caucasus as Muhammad Said Bey, or Said-Bek Shamil was a North Caucasian politician and émigré leader. The grandson of rebel leader Imam Shamil, Shamil was the monarch of the North Caucasian Emirate during the 1920–1921 Dagestan uprising before later going into exile. He was one of the leading figures of Prometheism, a Polish-led political project seeking to bring about the disintegration of the Soviet Union, and participated in several political projects by North Caucasian émigrés such as the Committee for the Independence of the Caucasus and the People's Party of Caucasian Highlanders.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in Prometheism and leader of the North Caucasian Emirate, Mehmed Said Şamil played a significant role in shaping regional politics during the 1920s. His involvement in various émigré projects had lasting impacts on the modern history of the Caucasus region.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key figure in Prometheism and leader of the North Caucasian Emirate, Mehmed Said Şamil played a significant role in shaping regional politics during the Soviet era. His involvement in various émigré projects aimed to promote independence for the Caucasus region.
